issues.body:
Seen in the Formbricks discovery lab (run 4, `ayme mcp` 0.1.0-alpha.0, worktree `a805c3a`), survey list page, row options menu ("Open options"), which has a Radix `DropdownMenuSub` "Change status" with `menuitemradio` items (`data-testid="survey-status-option-<status>"`).

## What happens

A Page Object action, run through `ayme mcp`:

```ts
await this.statusSubmenu.hover({ timeout: 30_000 });               // or .click(): both open the submenu
await this.page.getByTestId("survey-status-option-completed").click({ timeout: 30_000 });
```

- With `hover`: the MCP call ran past 60 s (client timeout); the survey's status did not change, the submenu was closed afterwards (`data-state="closed"` on the trigger).
- With `click` on the trigger, then `click` on the item (300 s client timeout): `TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded. No elements found for locator page.locator("internal:testid=[data-testid=\"survey-status-option-completed\"s]")`, and the call log says `locator resolved to <div tabindex="-1" role="menuitemradio" … data-testid="survey-status-option-completed" …>` first. So the submenu opened, the item was found, and it was gone before the click reached it.
- The built-in `hover` tool on the same trigger answered after 56.6 s and did open the submenu.
- The same two steps through the host's Playwright (the rig's own Chromium page, same tab): `hover` 138 ms, `click` 738 ms, status changed.
- Workaround that works: open the submenu with a click, then `option.dispatchEvent("click")` (no pointer movement): the status changes, the call answers in 16 s.

## Why it matters

Radix closes a submenu when the pointer leaves its trigger in a direction other than the submenu, or after a grace period. An action that moves to the item the way a user does should land; here it never does, so any submenu (status, "Change question type", "Add question below", "Move question to block") cannot be driven with plain `click`, and the failure reads as "No elements found" though the element was there a moment before.

On this page every click took ~40 s (row options trigger 42 s, built-in `click` on a filter button 37 s), so this may be downstream of the slow clicks tracked elsewhere (#957, #846); the submenu closing is the visible consequence. Evidence: `dogfood/formbricks-discovery/run-4/calls.jsonl` (marker `LIST status+archive`), `status-submenu-timeout.png`.

issues.title: A Page Object action that opens a Radix submenu and clicks its item fails: the submenu closes before the click lands

issues.body:
Seen in live page object discovery run 6 on Formbricks (ayme `a805c3a`, `@ayme-dev/mcp` 0.1.0-alpha.0, `ayme mcp` through the dogfood rig, headless Chromium). Page-tool time, not a slow page: the same click from Playwright in the rig takes 0.2 s.

## Setup

Formbricks survey list. Each row is a collection item `SurveyRow` (CSS root `div.relative.block:has([data-testid=survey-dropdown-trigger])`) with two actions that have availability predicates. Both predicates read `this.container.getByRole("link").getAttribute("href")`. Clicking a row's "Open options" opens a Radix dropdown menu, which marks the rest of the page `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`.

## Measurements (same element: row 0's "Open options")

| Rows rendered | Page Object `surveys.openOptions` | Built-in `click` (ref) | `press_key Escape` (menu closes) | Plain Playwright `click()` from the rig |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (list filtered) | 6.5 s | – | 2.5 s | 0.22 s |
| 7 | 42.9 s | 42.7 s / 42.8 s | 14.8 s | 0.24 s |
| 12 | 73.1 s | 73.0 s | 24.9 s | 0.20 s |
| 15 (after Load more) | 91.4 s | – | 31.2 s | – |

That's ~6.1 s per row to open, ~2.1 s per row to close. On the same page, at 7 rows:

- `snapshot` 0.14 s, `ayme_list_tools` 2 ms.
- A Page Object action that only reads the heading's text (`probeRead`, added for the test): 0.5–0.75 s.
- A built-in `hover` on the trigger: 0.75 s.
- The 93 s `TemplateGalleryPage.useTemplate(name)` on a 52-card gallery (cards are collection items too) may be the same pattern; run 5 saw 10 s with 26 cards.

So the cost comes only with the modal layer, it grows linearly with the number of collection items, and built-in tools pay it too.

**Changing only the predicates' locator** to CSS (`this.container.locator("a").first()`) brought `openOptions` at 7 rows from 42.9 s down to **1.0 s** (Escape 0.8 s).

**Counting predicate calls** (a `console.debug` in the predicate, 1 row): before the click, 4 observations × 2 predicates at 0 ms each. After the menu opened, **6 calls of 1001–1002 ms each, one after another** (3 observations × 2 predicates), which is the 6 s for that row. The Escape call shows the same in reverse.

While the menu is open, `ayme_list_tools` lists every row tool as `unavailable: a click would not reach it`. So the predicates' answers (or their timeouts) aren't used at all.

Server stderr and the browser console showed nothing during these calls besides page connect/disconnect and Formbricks's own warnings.

## Likely cause (read after measuring)

- `pomTree.ts` `observeInstance` asks `askPredicates(instance, tools)` whenever the instance is present (`if (observed.present) …`), even when its root is present but a click would not reach it. `availabilityOf` (pomInstance.ts) then puts the unreachable root first and never reads the answers.
- `askPredicates` awaits each predicate in turn, across instances too, with no time budget. Behind a modal layer, a predicate that reads a role locator finds nothing (#961), so every locator read waits for the full 1 s action timeout.
- The post-action settle observes several times (3 here), so a call costs items × predicates × observations × 1 s.

## Why it matters

Any list with a row menu becomes unusable: 1–1.5 min per menu open at 12–15 rows. An agent's MCP client times out (the SDK default is 60 s; run 4 hit `MCP error -32001: Request timed out`), and the agent cannot tell that the page itself is fast. The Page Object author did nothing unusual: the skill recommends role locators, and the predicates are trivial.

## Expected

Opening a menu costs about what it costs without Ayme, and doesn't grow by seconds per collection item. For example, a predicate isn't asked while its instance's root is unreachable (its answer wouldn't be used), or predicate reads don't wait out the action timeout during observation.

Related: #961 (same trigger, wrong reason), #846 (slow calls on very large pages, a different cause: element count), #957.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

**Triage (unattended, policy: vacation plan 3d): `bug`, `ready-for-agent`.** Kept the filer's labels; attached as a sub-issue of the layer-over-the-page tracking issue (#759), since the cost only appears while a modal layer is open.

**Verified by code path** (main `a805c3a`): `observeInstance` in `packages/ayme/src/pomTree.ts:383-387` calls `askPredicates` whenever the instance is present, including when its root is present but unreachable; `askPredicates` (`packages/ayme/src/pomInstance.ts:170-190`) awaits each predicate in turn with no budget. Behind a modal layer a role-locator read waits out the 1 s action timeout, so a call costs items × predicates × observations × 1 s, and the answers are then discarded because the unreachable root decides availability. The reporter's predicate-call counts match this.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Don't ask an instance's availability predicates when its root is unreachable; their answers aren't used and each can cost a full action timeout.

**Current behavior:** with a Radix modal menu open over a 12-row list, opening the menu takes 73 s (0.2 s in plain Playwright), growing ~6 s per collection item; built-in tools pay it too because they share the post-action observation.

**Desired behavior:** during observation, an instance whose Page Object Root is present but a click would not reach it is reported unavailable with the runtime's reason ("a click would not reach it") without running its predicates. Opening the same menu costs about what it does without ayme and doesn't grow with the number of items. Listed availability and reasons must stay exactly as today (they already come from the unreachable root).

**Key interfaces:**
- `observeInstance` in the Page Object tree observation
- `askPredicates` / `availabilityOf` in the Page Object instance module

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Browser test: with a modal layer covering a collection, no predicate of a covered item runs during observation (count calls).
- [ ] Items whose root is reachable still get their predicates asked and their reasons shown.
- [ ] Existing availability tests pass unchanged.

**Out of scope:**
- Root-less page Page Objects behind a layer and the false app reason they show ("Behind a modal layer, an availability predicate that reads a role locator gets absent…", #961, and #730). That needs a decision; this fix only covers instances with a root.
- Running predicates in parallel or with a time budget (possible follow-up if root-less cases stay slow).

issues.title: Opening a menu over a list takes ~6 s per collection item: availability predicates are asked serially, each waiting out the 1 s action timeout, though the root is unreachable

fix.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"enekesabel"} -->
_Requested by **Abel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01L8Mmq41SgWv7mFAFtaWAJc?thread=cmsg_01L8Mmq41SgWv7mFAFtaWAJcHdqSbrgz3os161Tth8bwJ6)_

Closes #962 (opening a menu over a list costs ~6 s per collection item).

## Summary

A Page Object Root a click would not reach already decides Action Availability before any predicate (ADR-0035), so its predicates' answers were never used. Behind a modal layer each role-locator read in them waited out the 1 s action timeout, per item × predicate × observation.

```diff
 observeInstance
   askPresence
   observeRoot
   observed.present = root.present
-  if present
+  if present and root (if any) is reachable
     askPredicates
```

Listed availability and reasons are unchanged: a covered item still shows "a click would not reach it; eN is in the way". Root-less Page Objects behind a layer (#961) are untouched, as the brief scopes.

## Evidence

New browser test in `actionAvailability.browser.test.ts`: two rows, a fixed dialog covering the second, a predicate that records which row it was asked about.

```text
expect(asked).toContain("open")
expect(asked).not.toContain("covered")
rows[0] → unavailable, "open is read-only"   (predicate reason still shown)
rows[1] → unavailable, "a click would not reach it; eN is in the way"
```

- **Before:** `AssertionError: expected [ Array(4) ] to not include 'covered'`
- **After:** passes; `actionAvailability.browser.test.ts` 26/26, ayme browser suite 530/530, unit 505/505.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** observation

An instance whose root is unreachable now has an empty `predicates` map. Nothing reads it in that state; `sameInstance` compares it, so a root going from covered to reachable still counts as a change and notifies.
